prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro CBTC (peak/off-peak/engineering hours). Degraded: LTC declares when MA, localization, point detection, platform interface or radio is untrusted (loss of trust treated like loss of comms); trains stationary/controlled speed until separation restored; controller action needed before automatic departure. Triage: safety critical, service affecting, cyber, maintenance-only. Return to automatic needs stable comms, verified route state, confirmed train position, recorded maintenance-to-operations handback; cybersecurity controls are prerequisites. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (LTC, OCC; selects holding/skip-stop/turnback/run-through via Lantern; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; receives Route Release Exception List; no vital intervention; starts manual route recovery confirming positions by independent indications/verbal reports; concurs with Maple on resets affecting route/occupancy). Revenue Train Operator (acknowledgements to Atlas; repeats back limit, max speed, stopping point, platform-clear instructions; in restricted manual handles speed/stopping/doors; sends Test Train Clearance Memo after proving run). Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (verifies points, vacancy, local protection before manual route; uses Axle Counter Reset Request to restore failed section; remote read-only outside window). Cyber Security Officer (reviews auth failures, lockouts, abnormal access). Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern (sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas; never obscures safety alarms). Service Timetable Server. Passenger Information Gateway (messages match LTC-accepted limits). Voice Dispatch Console (authorizes restricted manual moves unless contingency comms invoked). North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (East Junction; applies TSR Notice after validation); South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (West Junction; inhibits auto routing in blocks under manual occupancy confirmation); both send MA. East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon (sends Axle Counter Reset Request; holds points locked until confirmation). West Junction Interlocking (sends Route Release Exception List; rejects routes conflicting with manual protected moves). Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel (restricted manual if no MA/low location confidence; Brake Curve Checksum Log). Dual Channel Odometer. Train Radio Modem (reports safe-data loss to Atlas). Wayside Radio Access Network, alias Saffron. Maintenance Diagnostic Server (cannot alter MA; evidence frozen). Quarry (alias, full name not given; tags diagnostic sessions with incident ID before restarts). Platform Screen Door Controller (protected local state if stopping accuracy unverified). Cryptographic Key Management Appliance (no bypass except emergency

New part:
S202: The Cyber Security Officer shall maintain continuous monitoring of security events from the Safety Data Communication Network, the Wayside Radio Access Network, and the Metro Operations Control System.
S203: Security monitoring shall correlate authentication failures, session resets, rejected messages, configuration changes, and abnormal timing patterns without altering any safety command path.
S204: Alerts affecting train control availability shall be classified using operational impact, affected territory, and whether the event could change train movement authority.
S205: The Line Traffic Controller shall be notified when a cybersecurity event requires a restriction on automatic operation or a change in communications mode.
S206: The Cyber Security Officer uses the audit file to investigate radio session continuity and to confirm that security monitoring records are complete.
S207: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall be the controlled source for operational certificates used by trainborne, wayside, control center, and maintenance components.
S208: Certificate issuance shall require approved asset identity, recorded software baseline, assigned operating domain, and confirmation that the requesting component is authorized for service.
S209: Certificate renewal shall be planned before expiry so that the Atlas Onboard Controller, Train Radio Modem, North District Zone Controller, South District Zone Controller, and West Junction Interlocking do not enter service with degraded trust.
S210: Falcon shall reject any control message with an invalid signature, an expired certificate, or a sequence value outside the accepted window.
S211: Revocation shall be available for a compromised device, a retired device, or a device whose maintenance history can no longer be reconciled with approved configuration records.
S212: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server shall not be used to bypass certificate checks or to create alternate trust paths into safety-related communications.
S213: Administrative access to the Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall require named accounts, multifactor authentication, separation of duties, and recorded approval for privileged changes.
S214: The Signal Maintenance Engineer may request access needed for fault isolation, but the Cyber Security Officer shall approve security-sensitive permissions before they are enabled.
S215: The Revenue Train Operator shall not be assigned cybersecurity administration duties during passenger service, although security warnings presented in the cab shall remain part of normal operating awareness.
S216: The Metro Operations Control System uses the Test Train Clearance Memo as a controlled prerequisite before accepting security exceptions for non-revenue movement in protected territory.
S217: Audit evidence shall include time-synchronized event records, access approvals, certificate actions, configuration changes, alarm acknowledgements, and operator instructions related to communications security.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
